title: Staged fallback bridge for gradual rollbacks across hosted / dedicated / private deployments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create an operational pattern and automated tooling (the 'staged fallback bridge') to perform tenant-aware, incremental rollbacks and hotfix rollouts simultaneously across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Focus on minimizing customer downtime and avoiding data residency or KV cache inconsistency while coordinating communications with affected customers.
background: We continue to see model rollout regressions where canary evaluation metrics diverge per-tenant and per-environment. Hosted rollbacks are straightforward, but Dedicated and Private customers have constraints (pinning, slower patch windows, or customer-managed upgrades). Recent incidents highlighted: (a) cache mismatch when a rollback touched model KV cache format; (b) customer confusion about which tenants were affected; (c) race conditions during cross-env fallback leading to increased tail latency.
goal: Produce a repeatable runbook and automation that: (1) safely isolates tenants for rollback or hotfix, (2) synchronizes fallback policies across environments without forcing immediate private upgrades, and (3) provides clear customer-facing status and rollback timelines.
acceptance_criteria: A documented runbook for staged fallback bridge covering hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
Automation that can target a named tenant or label and flip them to a fallback model variant within SLA (target 95th percentile < 3s additional latency)
KV cache compatibility checks and migration guard included in the rollback flow
Customer communication templates and tracking that surface to CS and SRE dashboards
A dry-run executed against a low-risk tenant set with telemetry validating expected behaviour
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: confirm regression with eval suite and per-tenant telemetry (regressions.json link in links).
2) Scope: identify affected tenants by tenant-label and query console per-route model pins.
3) Safety checks: run kv-compatibility-check tool for target model pair; if incompatible, route to hotpatch packaging flow.
4) Canary expansion freeze: stop progressive rollout to additional tenants and pause scheduling of new dedicated upgrades.
5) Staged fallback: flip fallback policy for a small tenant cohort to fallback-model-1 using feature-flagged routing, observe 30m telemetry window.
6) Gradual ramp: if metrics stable, expand cohorts (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with automated guardrails; for Dedicated/Private, push advisory and offer automated fallback proxy where applicable.
7) Hotfix path: if rollback unsafe, trigger hotfix packaging (build compatibility shim, backfill KV mappings) and validate in canary before broad rollout.
8) Communication: update incident channel, customer-facing status page, and notify customer success with expected timeline and action items.
9) Post-rollback verification: run end-to-end prompts and regression evals, reconcile token accounting, and close with postmortem notes.
10) Postmortem & follow-up: schedule remediation tickets for runtime/compatibility gaps discovered and update model onboarding checklist.
recent_activity: 2025-02-18: Initial triage findings — KV cache format mismatch observed between model v3.2 and v3.1 (noted by SRE).
2025-02-21: Design review with Runtime & Private teams — agreed fallback proxy concept for Private deployments.
2025-02-28: Built prototype automation to flip tenant routing using feature-flagged policies (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/1287).
2025-03-05: Performed internal dry-run on staging tenants; observed 1.8s median added latency for fallback path; telemetry dashboard updated.
2025-03-10: Customer success rehearsal for external communications; drafted templates and legal-approved messaging for Private customers.
open_questions: What SLA do Dedicated customers expect for rollback windows versus Hosted? (product to confirm)
Should Private deployments be offered an automated fallback proxy or only advisory steps to apply locally?
How should billing be reconciled if fallbacks increase token usage due to longer outputs?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache incompatibility causing inference errors — Mitigation: mandatory compatibility check and cache wipe/migration guarded by a deploy gate.
Risk: Customer confusion and churn — Mitigation: pre-approved CS templates, tenant-specific timelines, and optional hands-on assistance for enterprise tenants.
Risk: Rollback automation triggers cascading resource pressure — Mitigation: autoscaling policy adjustment, burst-qps caps for fallback cohorts.
notes_for_oncall: If a private tenant cannot accept automated fallback, escalate to Private-Eng lead and arrange an emergency upgrade window.
When flipping cohorts, ensure console trace-id is passed to CS for per-tenant debugging.
Use the safe-mode flag (--no-cache-migration) only if customers request minimal change; document consequences in ticket.
